links.comparator_used: Nonthinking mode on the same Qwen3-14B model (2×2 factorial with prompt detail)
links.outcome: Information coverage (%) on OSCE-inspired checklist across 66 simulated primary care cases
links.effect: Internal reasoning significantly associated with improved coverage in the 2-way repeated-measures ANOVA, with a significant prompt detail × reasoning interaction; detailed+thinking 72.3% (SD 14.3%) vs about 60% for thinking or detailed prompt alone and about 51%-54% for minimal nonthinking. Differences most pronounced for past medical and family history domains.
links.quote: In the factorial analysis of the 4 LLM configurations, both prompt detail and internal reasoning were significantly associated with improved information coverage, with a significant interaction between prompt detail and internal reasoning interaction.

links.comparator_used: Minimal prompt configurations and rule-based choice-mode baseline
links.outcome: Checklist-based information coverage in simulated chatbot medical history taking
links.effect: Detailed and thinking mode: 72.3% mean coverage (SD 14.3%); configurations using either thinking or detailed prompts alone: approximately 60%; minimal nonthinking and rule-based configurations: approximately 51%-54%; overall configuration difference P<.001. Factorial analysis found prompt detail significantly associated with improved information coverage, with a significant interaction with internal reasoning.
links.quote: In the factorial analysis of the 4 LLM configurations, both prompt detail and internal reasoning were significantly associated with improved information coverage, with a significant interaction between prompt detail and internal reasoning interaction.
